Consult Summary:
- 53-year-old with 1-week painless left elbow swelling and warmth; clinician impression of olecranon bursitis; NSAID initiated and labs arranged; advised red flags and follow-up after tests.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Left elbow swelling noticed ~1 week ago; feels like fluid; slightly warm; not painful; full range of motion.
- Associated symptoms: Mild discomfort “feels weird” adjacent to swelling; no known trauma; desk-based job; runs 2–3 times/week.
- Pertinent negatives: No severe pain; no significant tenderness at olecranon tip; no known injury; no prior similar episodes; denies eczema; unsure about family rheumatologic history (later says “No”).
- Past medical history: Osteoarthritis diagnosed by GP a few years ago.
- Allergies: Peanut allergy. No known medication allergies.
- Medications: None regularly.
- Social history: Desk job; physically active (running).

Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Findings: Visible swelling over left elbow. Skin noted to be a bit dry at the tip. Area slightly warmer than adjacent skin. Non-tender at olecranon tip; mild discomfort adjacent to swelling on palpation. Full movement reported. No features suggestive of septic arthritis per clinician’s assessment.

Impression:
- Left olecranon bursitis (non-septic appearance). Differential considerations to be screened include inflammatory/infectious causes and gout.

Plan:
- Medication: Ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily; route not documented. Take after food; stop if heartburn occurs.
- Tests: Blood tests to be arranged via mailed forms—checking inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatologic antibodies, and for gout. Results expected ~5–6 days after blood draw.
- Follow-up: Arrange follow-up after blood tests to review results and reassess joint; can be phone, video, or in-person per patient preference.
- Safety-netting: Seek urgent care if elbow becomes very red, very painful, or if redness spreads/worsens, due to concern for septic arthritis requiring immediate assessment and treatment.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Vitals; full review of systems; detailed musculoskeletal exam (erythema, fluctuation, precise ROM measurements); medication route for ibuprofen; comprehensive allergy/medication reconciliation beyond stated items; immunization and broader PMH not discussed.  
● Internal conflicts: Family history of rheumatologic disease—patient initially “not sure,” later “No” (conflict noted). Age stated as 53 with DOB given as 04/05/1973 (potential discrepancy; conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear, with occasional inaudible/ellipses; key clinical details captured.
